_notes: Handkuraterat 2026-08-27 mot broomfield.org (officiell källa för varje fält, se source_url per post). City Hall-adressen kryssverifierad mot AgendaLink API:ts egna room.address-fält för Council-möten (samma adress, oberoende källa). Öppettider för City Hall INTE publicerade någonstans som kontrollerats -- utelämnat (inte gissat). En ZIP-diskrepans för County Commons Park (80020 vs 80021) hittades i en första forskningsrunda; löst genom att läsa parkens EGEN sida direkt (80021) snarare än en sekundär sida som inte ens listade parken. Inga name_aliases seedade än -- Broomfield har ingen live events-källa (WebTrac blockerad, se configs/broomfield_co.json) att hämta riktiga skrapade venue-strängar ifrån, till skillnad från Moreno Valley/Brookings vars aliases kommer direkt ur verifierad skrapad data. Enda biblioteket i Broomfield -- ingen ytterligare gren att lägga till.

facilities.name: George Di Ciero City and County Building
facilities.description: The seat of Broomfield's consolidated city-county government, named for former City and County Manager George Di Ciero. Houses City Council chambers and administrative offices.

facilities.name: Mamie Doud Eisenhower Public Library
facilities.description: Broomfield's public library, named for Mamie Doud Eisenhower at the community's request. The current building opened November 10, 2001. Broomfield's only library location.

facilities.name: Paul Derda Recreation Center
facilities.description: An 85,000-square-foot city-operated indoor recreation facility within Broomfield County Commons Park, with an aquatic park, gymnastics center, gymnasiums, fitness/weight areas, and an indoor track.

facilities.name: Broomfield Community Center
facilities.description: A 98,000-square-foot city-operated facility combining fitness and aquatics amenities with dedicated space for Broomfield Senior Services and creative-arts programming, including a woodshop and pottery studio.

facilities.name: Broomfield County Commons
facilities.description: A 300-acre city-owned park complex with an 80-acre sports and playing-field area, 237 acres of open space, a cemetery, and the Paul Derda Recreation Center.
